steps.body: Chapter 2 fit a line; chapter 3 used it to predict. But real points don't sit ON the line — each one misses by some amount. That miss has a name: the residual, observed minus predicted. It is the line's error, measured point by point.

widget.prompt: The line is ŷ = 2x + 1. The data point is (3, 9). What is its residual, observed − predicted?

commonErrors.feedback: 7 is the PREDICTION. The residual is the gap: observed 9 minus predicted 7.
Order matters: observed − predicted = 9 − 7 = +2. Above the line is positive.

widget.fallbackFeedback: First run the line at x = 3 (that's the prediction), then subtract it from the observed 9.
widget.successFeedback: Predicted: 2·3 + 1 = 7. Observed: 9. Residual: 9 − 7 = +2 — the point floats 2 above the line.

steps.body: Place the point the residual describes.

widget.prompt: Under ŷ = 2x + 1, the line predicts 5 at x = 2. Plot the OBSERVED point whose residual is +1.

pointErrors.feedback: That is the PREDICTED point — it sits on the line, residual 0. Observed − predicted must come out +1.
One BELOW the line is residual −1. A positive leftover lives above the prediction.

widget.missFeedback: Residual = observed − predicted, so observed = 5 + 1 = 6: plot (2, 6).
widget.successFeedback: (2, 6): one above the line's 5 — a +1 leftover, which is all a residual is.

predict.prompt: A data point sits ABOVE the fitted line. Its residual is…

options.label: Positive — the world beat the prediction
Negative — being off is a deficit
Zero — the line already averaged it in

predict.reveal: Residual = observed − predicted: above the line means the observed value is bigger, so the residual is positive. The sign encodes WHICH WAY the line was wrong — that direction is data, not noise.

explanationVariants: Predicted at x = 5: 2·5 + 1 = 11. Observed 9 falls short, so the residual is 9 − 11 = −2.
Negative residuals mark points below the line — the prediction overshot.

widget.prompt: Same line ŷ = 2x + 1. What is the residual of (5, 9)?

commonErrors.feedback: Keep the sign: observed 9 sits BELOW predicted 11, so −2.
11 is the prediction. Subtract it from the observed: 9 − 11.

widget.successFeedback: 9 − 11 = −2: the line overpredicted by 2. Sign carries direction; size carries how badly.

explanationVariants: A residual of 0 means observed = predicted: the point lies exactly on the line.
Zero residual is a perfect hit — rare with real data, routine with made-up data.

widget.prompt: A point has residual 0. Where is it?

options.label: Exactly on the line
options.feedback: Observed equals predicted — no miss at all.

options.label: At the origin
options.feedback: The origin is about x and y being zero, not the miss being zero.

options.label: At the average of the data
options.feedback: The mean point often has a SMALL residual, but zero means on-the-line, wherever that is.

widget.successFeedback: Residuals measure distance from the LINE, not from zero or from the center of the data.

steps.body: Every data point gets a residual: positive above the line, negative below, zero on it. A fitted line doesn't erase the misses — it chooses where to put them. Reading those leftovers is how you audit the line.

explanationVariants: (1,4): predicted 3, residual +1. (2,4): predicted 5, residual −1. (4,12): predicted 9, residual +3 — the largest miss.
The biggest |residual| flags the point the line explains worst — the first outlier suspect.

widget.prompt: Under ŷ = 2x + 1, which point does the line miss WORST: (1,4), (2,4), or (4,12)?

options.label: (4, 12) — residual +3
options.feedback: Predicted 9, observed 12: a 3-unit miss, triple the others.

widget.successFeedback: Comparing |residuals| ranks the line's failures — the biggest one is your outlier candidate.

hints: Compute the point's residual under EACH line separately.
Line A ŷ = x + 2 at x = 4 predicts 6; line B ŷ = 3x − 2 predicts 10. The observed is 8.
Misses: |8 − 6| = 2 and |8 − 10| = 2 — equal size, opposite signs.
explanationVariants: The point (4, 8) misses line A by +2 and line B by −2 — the same distance from each, from opposite sides.
A single point can't crown a winner between two lines; whole residual SETS can. That's the next lesson.

widget.prompt: Point (4, 8). Line A: ŷ = x + 2. Line B: ŷ = 3x − 2. Which line misses it by less?

options.label: Neither
options.feedback: A predicts 6 (residual +2); B predicts 10 (residual −2). Equal misses, opposite directions.

options.label: Line A
options.feedback: A predicts 6: off by 2. But check B before deciding: it predicts 10 — also off by 2.

options.label: Line B
options.feedback: B predicts 10: off by 2. A predicts 6 — the same 2 the other way.

widget.successFeedback: One point rarely settles a fit. Judging lines takes the whole leftover collection — next lesson's job.

steps.body: The residual is the line's per-point error.
takeaways: Residual = observed − predicted: positive above the line, negative below, zero on it.
The sign says which way the line erred; the size says how badly.
The largest |residual| flags the point the model explains worst.
steps.teaser: Next: stop reading leftovers one at a time — their PATTERN tells you whether a line was the right tool at all.
